group.passage:
Drop an ice cube into a glass of water, and it will float. This seems perfectly normal, but it is actually rather strange. For most other substances, the solid form is packed more tightly than the liquid form, so a solid piece will [[1]] to the bottom of its own liquid. Water, however, is a well-known [[2]] to this rule.
The reason lies in how water molecules behave as the temperature drops. When water begins to [[3]] ice, its molecules lock together in a fixed, open pattern. This pattern leaves more empty [[4]] between the molecules than there is in liquid water. In other words, the freezing process causes water to [[5]]. As a result, a piece of ice is lighter than the same amount of liquid water, so it stays on top.
This unusual behavior is important for life in lakes and ponds. In winter, as the air above a lake gets colder, a [[6]] of ice forms on the surface first. Like a blanket, this ice helps [[7]] the water below from the freezing air. The deeper water therefore stays liquid, and fish and other creatures can remain [[8]] through the long winter. If ice went to the bottom instead, many lakes could freeze solid from the bottom up, and much of the life in them would die.
The same property explains why you should be [[9]] when you put a full glass bottle of water in the freezer. As the water freezes, it pushes hard against the glass and may even break it. Out at sea, the same property allows [[10]] icebergs to float, even though most of each iceberg lies below the surface.

translation_zh.text:
把一塊冰丟進一杯水裡，它會浮起來。這看似再正常不過，其實相當奇怪。對其他大多數物質來說，固態排列得比液態緊密，所以一塊固體會沉到同種液體的底部。然而，水是這條規則有名的例外。
原因在於溫度下降時水分子的表現。當水開始變成冰時，水分子會固定成一種開放的結構。這種結構讓分子之間留下的空隙比液態水時還多。換句話說，結冰的過程會讓水膨脹。結果，一塊冰比同體積的液態水還輕，所以會浮在上面。
這種不尋常的特性對湖泊和池塘裡的生物非常重要。冬天湖面上的空氣變冷時，湖面會先結起一層冰。這層冰像毯子一樣，幫助保護下方的湖水不受寒冷空氣影響。因此較深處的水仍保持液態，魚和其他生物得以在漫長的冬天裡存活。如果冰反而沉到底部，許多湖泊可能會從底部往上整個凍結，湖中大部分的生物都會死亡。
同樣的特性也說明了為什麼把裝滿水的玻璃瓶放進冷凍庫時要小心。水結冰時會用力擠壓玻璃，甚至可能把瓶子撐破。在海上，同樣的特性讓巨大的冰山也能漂浮，雖然每座冰山大部分都位於水面之下。
